newsitem.title: USA: Maine tax on New Hampshire company upheld.
newsitem.headline: Maine tax on New Hampshire company upheld.

text.p: Maine Supreme Court dismissed Tuesday claims by a New Hampshire granite quarry that its sales to Maine customers should not be subjected to Maine's sales and use taxes.

The court rejected the claim by John Swenson Granite Inc that Maine could not tax the stone it sold to Maine customers because the transaction occurred at the company's facility in New Hampshire -- which has no general sales tax.
The justices ruled unanimously that because Swenson used its own trucks to deliver most of the stone to Maine the transactions occured at the delivery point and were subject to the state's sales tax.

The court acknowledged that when common carrier trucks were used the sales transaction occurred in New Hampshire, but the justices ruled the product was nevertheless subject to the use tax -- which complements the sales tax on goods purchased out of state.
Swenson, based in Concord, New Hampshire, filed suit after Maine moved to collect tax and penalties on more than $4 million in sales in Maine between April 1, 1984, and December 31, 1989.
